title: Genesis Chapter 47 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Genesis chapter 47 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Genesis Chapter 47 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Genesis Chapter 47.

questions.question: Who came and told Pharaoh about his father and brethren arriving in Egypt?
questions.correctAnswer: Joseph
questions.explanation: Joseph came and told Pharaoh about his father and brethren, as stated in Genesis 47:1.

questions.question: How many of Joseph's brethren did he present to Pharaoh?
questions.correctAnswer: Five
questions.explanation: Joseph took five men of his brethren and presented them to Pharaoh according to Genesis 47:2.

questions.question: What occupation did Joseph's brethren tell Pharaoh they had?
questions.correctAnswer: Shepherds
questions.explanation: Joseph's brethren said they were shepherds, both they and their fathers, as recorded in Genesis 47:3.

questions.question: Why did Joseph's brethren ask Pharaoh to let them dwell in the land of Goshen?
options: Because they wanted to build a city
Because their flocks had no pasture due to famine in Canaan
Because they wanted to work in Pharaoh’s palace
Because they wanted to trade goods
questions.correctAnswer: Because their flocks had no pasture due to famine in Canaan
questions.explanation: They requested to dwell in Goshen because their flocks had no pasture due to the severe famine in Canaan, as stated in Genesis 47:4.

questions.question: What did Pharaoh command Joseph regarding his father and brethren?
options: To send them back to Canaan
To make them dwell in the best land in Egypt, specifically Goshen
To give them gold and silver
To make them work in the fields
questions.correctAnswer: To make them dwell in the best land in Egypt, specifically Goshen
questions.explanation: Pharaoh instructed Joseph to make his father and brethren dwell in the best land of Egypt, in the land of Goshen, as recorded in Genesis 47:6.

questions.question: Who did Joseph bring before Pharaoh to be presented?
questions.correctAnswer: His father Jacob
questions.explanation: Joseph brought in his father Jacob and set him before Pharaoh, as detailed in Genesis 47:7.

questions.question: What was Jacob’s response to Pharaoh when asked his age?
questions.correctAnswer: One hundred and thirty years
questions.explanation: Jacob told Pharaoh that his days were one hundred and thirty years, as stated in Genesis 47:9.

questions.question: Did Jacob bless Pharaoh before leaving his presence?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jacob blessed Pharaoh and then went out from before him, as recorded in Genesis 47:10.

questions.question: In which land did Joseph give his father and brethren possession?
questions.correctAnswer: Land of Rameses
questions.explanation: Joseph gave them possession in the land of Egypt, in the best of the land, specifically in the land of Rameses, as commanded by Pharaoh in Genesis 47:11.

questions.question: True or False: Joseph nourished only his father with bread according to their families.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Joseph nourished his father, his brethren, and all his father's household with bread according to their families, as seen in Genesis 47:12.

questions.question: True or False: The famine was so severe that both Egypt and Canaan fainted because of it.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Genesis 47:13 states the famine was very sore, so that Egypt and all the land of Canaan fainted because of the famine.

questions.question: Which request came first according to Genesis 47:18-19?
options: Requesting seed to sow the land
Requesting to buy their land and themselves as servants
Requesting more bread because money was spent
questions.correctAnswer: Requesting more bread because money was spent
questions.explanation: First, they admitted their money was spent and asked for bread; then later they requested to sell themselves and their land to Pharaoh, as narrated in Genesis 47:18-19.

questions.question: How did Joseph deal with the famine when the money failed in Egypt?
options: He gave up and stopped feeding people
He asked people to bring their cattle and exchanged bread for it
He asked Pharaoh to send help
He sent people back to Canaan
questions.correctAnswer: He asked people to bring their cattle and exchanged bread for it
questions.explanation: Joseph instructed people to give their cattle in exchange for bread when money failed, according to Genesis 47:16.

questions.question: True or False: Pharaoh bought all the land of Egypt himself during the famine.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Joseph bought all the land of Egypt for Pharaoh because the famine caused the Egyptians to sell their fields, as stated in Genesis 47:20.

questions.question: What portion of the produce was to be given to Pharaoh according to Joseph's law?
questions.correctAnswer: One fifth
questions.explanation: Joseph established that Pharaoh should have the fifth part (one fifth) of the produce, as recorded in Genesis 47:24 and 47:26.

medium.title: Genesis Chapter 47 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Genesis Chapter 47 to real-life situations.

questions.question: How did Joseph provide for his family during the famine according to Genesis 47?
options: He gave them money to buy food
He nourished them with bread according to their families
He sent them back to Canaan
He made them work for Pharaoh
questions.correctAnswer: He nourished them with bread according to their families
questions.explanation: Genesis 47:12 states that Joseph nourished his father, brethren, and household with bread according to their families, showing his care and provision during the famine.

questions.question: What was the condition of the land of Egypt and Canaan during the famine?
options: Only Egypt was affected by famine
Both lands fainted by reason of the famine
The famine was mild and manageable
questions.correctAnswer: Both lands fainted by reason of the famine
questions.explanation: Genesis 47:13 explains that the famine was very sore, causing both Egypt and Canaan to faint, emphasizing the severe hardship faced during this time.

questions.question: What did Joseph do with all the money found in Egypt and Canaan for the corn they bought?
options: He returned it to the people
He brought it into Pharaoh's house
He used it to pay his family
questions.correctAnswer: He brought it into Pharaoh's house
questions.explanation: Genesis 47:14 states that Joseph gathered all the money found in Egypt and Canaan for the corn and brought it into Pharaoh's house, showing his stewardship and loyalty to Pharaoh.

questions.question: True or False: When the money failed in Egypt and Canaan, the people stopped coming to Joseph for bread.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Genesis 47:15 indicates that when money failed, all the Egyptians came to Joseph asking for bread, showing their dependence on him during the famine.

questions.question: What did Joseph request from the Egyptians when their money failed?
questions.correctAnswer: Their cattle
questions.explanation: According to Genesis 47:16, Joseph asked the Egyptians to give their cattle in exchange for bread if their money failed, displaying a fair barter system during the famine.

questions.question: What did Joseph exchange bread for from the people?
questions.correctAnswer: Horses, flocks, cattle, and asses
questions.explanation: Genesis 47:17 mentions that Joseph gave bread in exchange for horses, flocks, cattle of herds, and asses, indicating the broad range of livestock traded during the famine.

questions.question: What did the people say to Joseph after their money and cattle were spent?
options: We have nothing left but our bodies and lands
We will stop asking for bread
questions.correctAnswer: We have nothing left but our bodies and lands
questions.explanation: Genesis 47:18 records the people's words that their money and cattle were gone, and only their bodies and lands remained, illustrating their desperation.

questions.question: Based on Genesis 47:19-20, what did Joseph do when the people offered themselves and their lands to Pharaoh for bread?
options: He bought all the land of Egypt for Pharaoh
He offered them jobs in Pharaoh’s palace
questions.correctAnswer: He bought all the land of Egypt for Pharaoh
questions.explanation: Genesis 47:19-20 shows Joseph's purchase of all Egyptian land for Pharaoh because the famine forced the people to sell their fields, demonstrating Joseph's role in centralizing land under Pharaoh.

questions.question: True or False: Joseph sold the land of the priests to Pharaoh during the famine.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Genesis 47:22 states that only the priests' lands were not bought by Joseph because the priests had a portion assigned by Pharaoh, so they did not sell their lands.

questions.question: What does Genesis 47:21 teach about Joseph’s leadership over the people after buying their land?
options: He enslaved the people in one city
He removed the people to cities across Egypt
He allowed the people to stay in their lands
questions.correctAnswer: He removed the people to cities across Egypt
questions.explanation: Genesis 47:21 reveals that Joseph relocated the people to cities throughout Egypt, indicating an organized resettlement under his governance.

questions.question: How does the passage from Genesis 47:12-24 teach about trusting in God during difficult times?
options: By showing Joseph’s provision and management during famine
By encouraging people to hoard resources
By advising people to leave Egypt immediately
By telling people to rely solely on their own strength
questions.correctAnswer: By showing Joseph’s provision and management during famine
questions.explanation: The passage demonstrates faith and trust in God through Joseph’s wise stewardship and provision for his family and the nation during severe famine (Genesis 47:12-24).

questions.question: What does Genesis 47:23-24 promise will happen if the people sow the land with the seed given by Joseph?
options: They will lose their lands to Pharaoh
They will give the fifth part to Pharaoh and keep four parts for themselves
They will have to leave Egypt
They will starve despite sowing the land
questions.correctAnswer: They will give the fifth part to Pharaoh and keep four parts for themselves
questions.explanation: Genesis 47:23-24 explains that if the people sow the land with seed provided, they will give one-fifth of the produce to Pharaoh and keep four-fifths for their own food and households.

questions.question: True or False: According to Genesis 47:25, the people recognized that Joseph had saved their lives and willingly became servants to Pharaoh.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Genesis 47:25 shows the people's gratitude and willingness to serve Pharaoh because Joseph had saved their lives through his provision during famine.

questions.question: How does the interaction between Joseph and the Egyptians over money and land in Genesis 47 illustrate biblical principles about stewardship and dependence on God?
options: It shows the dangers of trusting others
It teaches us to use resources wisely and depend on God’s provision
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches us to use resources wisely and depend on God’s provision
questions.explanation: The passage (Genesis 47:14-22) reveals Joseph’s wise management of resources and how the people came to depend on God’s provision through Joseph, demonstrating stewardship and trust.

questions.question: What practical lesson about humility and obedience can believers learn from Jacob’s request to Joseph in Genesis 47:29-31?
options: To demand their own way in all matters
To plan for the future and submit to God’s will
questions.correctAnswer: To plan for the future and submit to God’s will
questions.explanation: Jacob’s request to Joseph to bury him with his fathers (Genesis 47:29-31) shows humility and obedience in honoring family and God's promises, encouraging believers to trust and plan wisely.

hard.title: Genesis Chapter 47 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Genesis Chapter 47.

questions.question: What portion of their produce did Joseph decree that the people of Egypt must give to Pharaoh?
questions.correctAnswer: One fifth
questions.explanation: Genesis 47:24 states that the people shall give the fifth part unto Pharaoh as a tax or tribute.

questions.question: Which portion of the land did Joseph specifically not buy for Pharaoh during the famine?
questions.correctAnswer: The land of the priests
questions.explanation: Genesis 47:22 explains that Joseph did not buy the land of the priests because they had a portion assigned of Pharaoh and ate their portion.

questions.question: How long did Jacob live in the land of Egypt according to Genesis 47?
questions.correctAnswer: Seventeen years
questions.explanation: Genesis 47:28 states that Jacob lived in Egypt for seventeen years before his death.

questions.question: What did Joseph provide to the people along with buying their land to enable them to continue farming?
questions.correctAnswer: Seed
questions.explanation: Genesis 47:23 says Joseph gave seed to the people so they could sow the land after he bought their land for Pharaoh.

questions.question: What was Israel's (Jacob's) request to Joseph before he died?
options: To bury him with his fathers outside Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: To bury him with his fathers outside Egypt
questions.explanation: Genesis 47:29-30 records Jacob asking Joseph not to bury him in Egypt but to carry him out and bury him in the family burial place.

questions.question: How did Joseph respond to the famine when money was no longer available to buy bread?
options: He imported grain from other lands
questions.correctAnswer: He exchanged bread for cattle
questions.explanation: Genesis 47:16-17 shows Joseph taking livestock in exchange for bread when the people ran out of money.

questions.question: According to Genesis 47, what was the occupation of Joseph's brethren when they came to Egypt?
questions.correctAnswer: Shepherds
questions.explanation: Genesis 47:3 states Joseph's brethren identified themselves as shepherds, as were their fathers.

questions.question: Which land was given to Joseph's family to dwell in Egypt?
questions.correctAnswer: Land of Rameses
questions.explanation: Genesis 47:11 records that Joseph gave his family possession in the land of Rameses as Pharaoh commanded.

questions.question: What was the significance of Joseph putting his hand under Jacob's thigh before his death?
options: A symbolic act of blessing and oath
questions.correctAnswer: A symbolic act of blessing and oath
questions.explanation: Genesis 47:29 shows Jacob asking Joseph to put his hand under his thigh as a sign of a solemn oath, a common ancient Near Eastern practice for confirming promises.

questions.question: True or False: Joseph made a law that Pharaoh should receive a tenth of the produce from the land of Egypt.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Genesis 47:26 clearly states Pharaoh received a fifth part, not a tenth, as a law made by Joseph.

questions.question: True or False: Joseph's policy of acquiring land and servants for Pharaoh during the famine prefigures the establishment of a centralized state in Egypt.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Genesis 47:20-21 describes Joseph buying all the land and moving people to cities, which historically aligns with the consolidation of power under Pharaoh, a theme echoed in Exodus 1:11.

questions.question: Which biblical passage echoes the theme of Joseph’s administration and provision during famine as seen in Genesis 47?
questions.explanation: Psalm 105:16-22 recounts Joseph’s rise to power and provision during famine, directly echoing Genesis 47's narrative.

questions.question: In literary terms, what device is used in Genesis 47:29-31 with Jacob’s request regarding burial and Joseph’s oath?
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio
questions.explanation: The passage forms an inclusio by opening and closing with the burial request and oath, framing the narrative and emphasizing the importance of the burial promise.

questions.question: Which Hebrew word in Genesis 47 meaning 'seed' is significant for understanding agricultural promises in this chapter?
questions.correctAnswer: Zera
questions.explanation: 'Zera' (זֶרַע) means 'seed' in Hebrew and is used in Genesis 47:23-24 to denote the agricultural seed given to the people to sow the land.

questions.question: How does Genesis 47:27-28 demonstrate fulfillment of the Abrahamic covenant in the context of Israel's settlement in Egypt?
options: Through Israel's multiplication and possession of land
questions.correctAnswer: Through Israel's multiplication and possession of land
questions.explanation: Genesis 47:27 shows Israel grew and multiplied in Egypt, fulfilling God's promise to Abraham of numerous descendants and possession of land, a theme reiterated in Genesis 12:7.

theological.title: Genesis Chapter 47 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Genesis Chapter 47 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What divine attribute is demonstrated by Pharaoh's invitation for Joseph's family to dwell in the best land of Egypt, specifically Goshen?
questions.correctAnswer: God's providence
questions.explanation: Genesis 47:6 shows Pharaoh instructing Joseph to settle his family in the best land, the land of Goshen, indicating God's providential care in providing refuge and sustenance during famine.

questions.question: How does Genesis 47:13-14 reveal a doctrine about human dependence in times of trial?
options: Humans must rely on their own strength during famine
God sovereignly controls economic resources to test faith
Famine causes people to turn to false gods
Survival depends on political power alone
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly controls economic resources to test faith
questions.explanation: Verses 13-14 describe severe famine and Joseph gathering all money for grain, reflecting God's sovereign control over resources to direct human reliance on His provision (cf. Deut 8:3).

questions.question: What theological truth about sin and human fallenness is implied by the Egyptians selling their lands and becoming servants to Pharaoh?
options: Sin results in loss of autonomy and servitude
Sin has no effect on economic status
Sin is unrelated to material possessions
questions.correctAnswer: Sin results in loss of autonomy and servitude
questions.explanation: Genesis 47:20-21 shows famine-induced poverty leading to selling lands and servitude, reflecting the doctrine that sin brings bondage and loss of original dominion (cf. Romans 6:16).

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Joseph’s accumulation of power over Egypt was mere political opportunism. What does Genesis 47:23-24 actually teach about the nature of this arrangement?
options: Joseph exploited the people for personal wealth
Joseph established a divinely ordained economic system for survival
Joseph ignored the famine and let people starve
Joseph's actions led to rebellion and chaos
questions.correctAnswer: Joseph established a divinely ordained economic system for survival
questions.explanation: Verses 23-24 show Joseph buying the land for Pharaoh but allowing people to keep four-fifths of the produce, instituting a just system preserving life, reflecting God's providential governance (cf. Prov 8:15-16).

questions.question: What doctrinal insight about God's faithfulness to His promises can be drawn from Jacob’s interaction with Pharaoh and his settling in Egypt?
options: God abandons His people in exile
God’s promises extend beyond Canaan into Egypt
God’s covenant is limited to the land of Canaan only
questions.correctAnswer: God’s promises extend beyond Canaan into Egypt
questions.explanation: Genesis 47:7-10 and 27-28 reveal Jacob blessing Pharaoh and dwelling in Egypt, showing God's faithfulness to preserve His people even outside the promised land, a foreshadowing of future deliverance (cf. Exodus 3:7-8).

questions.question: How does Joseph’s acceptance of land and servants for Pharaoh during famine reveal a broader biblical teaching on stewardship and authority?
options: Authority is based solely on military conquest
Stewardship involves exercising authority for the welfare of others
Authority is unrelated to divine mandate
questions.correctAnswer: Stewardship involves exercising authority for the welfare of others
questions.explanation: Genesis 47:16-17 shows Joseph exchanging bread for cattle and managing resources, demonstrating stewardship under God's authority to sustain life, aligning with biblical principles of godly leadership (cf. 1 Peter 4:10).

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most clearly demonstrated by Joseph’s sustaining of his family and all Egypt during famine?
questions.correctAnswer: Mercy
questions.explanation: Genesis 47:12 indicates Joseph nourished his father and brethren with bread during famine, showing God's mercy in providing sustenance through Joseph (cf. Psalm 86:15).

questions.question: What does the exemption of the priests’ land from being sold to Pharaoh teach about the intersection of sacred office and economic realities?
options: Sacred office is irrelevant to economic matters
Divine provision protects those serving in sacred roles
Priests were wealthy and unaffected by famine
questions.correctAnswer: Divine provision protects those serving in sacred roles
questions.explanation: Genesis 47:22 states the priests did not sell their land because Pharaoh assigned them a portion, demonstrating God's provision for the priestly role even amid crisis (cf. Numbers 18:21).

questions.question: How does the relocation of the people to cities across Egypt (Genesis 47:21) contribute to the theme of God's sovereign control over human history?
options: God abandons His control in political matters
God orchestrates human events for His purposes
God is limited by human decisions
questions.correctAnswer: God orchestrates human events for His purposes
questions.explanation: Genesis 47:21 shows people moved throughout Egypt, illustrating God's sovereign orchestration of history to preserve His covenant people and prepare for future redemption (cf. Acts 17:26).

questions.question: What is the theological significance of Jacob’s request to be buried with his fathers rather than in Egypt?
options: It reflects hope in resurrection and covenant continuity
It indicates a lack of trust in God’s provision
questions.correctAnswer: It reflects hope in resurrection and covenant continuity
questions.explanation: Genesis 47:29-30 reveals Jacob’s desire to be buried in Canaan, symbolizing faith in God’s promises beyond death and continuity of the covenant, a foreshadowing of resurrection hope (cf. Hebrews 11:13-16).

questions.question: Combining Genesis 47:3-4 and Genesis 47:27, what does the chapter teach about God’s preservation of His covenant people amidst hardship?
options: God allows His people to perish in famine
God preserves His people by providing refuge and multiplication
God’s covenant is conditional on perfect obedience
God’s people become isolated and diminished
questions.correctAnswer: God preserves His people by providing refuge and multiplication
questions.explanation: Verses 3-4 describe the family seeking refuge in Goshen as shepherds, and verse 27 shows Israel dwelling and multiplying there, illustrating God's preservation and blessing despite trials (cf. Genesis 12:2-3).

questions.question: What combined doctrinal teaching about God’s justice and mercy is conveyed by Joseph buying all the land for Pharaoh (Genesis 47:20) and setting a law for a fifth part tribute (Genesis 47:26)?
options: God’s justice leads to harsh oppression without mercy
God’s justice is tempered with mercy to sustain the people
questions.correctAnswer: God’s justice is tempered with mercy to sustain the people
questions.explanation: Joseph’s acquisition of land for Pharaoh (v.20) and instituting a fifth tribute (v.26) show God's justice in rightful authority balanced with mercy allowing survival, reflecting biblical justice and mercy (cf. Micah 6:8).

questions.question: What does Joseph’s role in Genesis 47 teach about the doctrine of providential mediation in salvation history?
options: God works through human agents to accomplish His purposes
God acts only through direct supernatural intervention
Human actions are irrelevant to God’s plan
Salvation is purely individual and not corporate
questions.correctAnswer: God works through human agents to accomplish His purposes
questions.explanation: Joseph’s leadership in managing famine relief (throughout chapter 47) exemplifies God's providence working through chosen human mediators to preserve His covenant people (cf. Romans 8:28).

questions.question: How does the narrative arc of Genesis 47 connect to the broader biblical theme of exile and redemption?
options: It shows permanent rejection from God's promises
It foreshadows Israel’s temporary exile and eventual redemption
It denies any future hope for the covenant people
It emphasizes isolation from the covenant
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows Israel’s temporary exile and eventual redemption
questions.explanation: The chapter’s depiction of Israel dwelling in Egypt (v.27-28) sets the stage for the Exodus, the key biblical redemption event, illustrating God's faithfulness through exile to restoration (cf. Deuteronomy 6:20-25).

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about human stewardship and God’s provision is highlighted by Joseph giving seed to the people so they could sow the land (Genesis 47:23-24)?
options: God provides all things for idleness
God requires responsible stewardship in cooperation with His provision
God’s provision is automatic without human effort
Human work is irrelevant to survival
questions.correctAnswer: God requires responsible stewardship in cooperation with His provision
questions.explanation: Joseph’s provision of seed (v.23-24) coupled with the command to sow shows that God’s provision invites human cooperation through stewardship, consistent with biblical teaching on labor and provision (cf. 2 Thessalonians 3:10).
